natural_language_statement: Given an algebra homomorphism φ from a multivariate polynomial ring to E and an ideal Q in that polynomial ring, polynomialJacobian sends a vector t to the function on Q given by summing φ of each partial derivative times the corresponding coordinate of t; polynomialTangent is its kernel, and PolynomialNormal is the quotient by that submodule. A derivation that annihilates Q after applying φ yields a vector in polynomialTangent. If every vector in that tangent submodule has zero i-coordinate, then the derivation D C E sends φ(X i) to zero.
explanation: The bundle defines the linear Jacobian map, its tangent kernel, and the resulting quotient space. It relates derivations to tangent vectors and uses coordinate vanishing on the entire tangent space to conclude vanishing of the corresponding universal derivation value.
